clue.text: Commons vote leads to disagreement

definitions.meaning: in the House of Commons members vote by physically separating into two lobbies
a split or rift between people who differ

explanation.surface: A vote in Parliament ends up causing a falling-out.
explanation.walkthrough: The House of Commons is the elected chamber of the UK Parliament, where a formal vote is called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a formal parliamentary vote and a split in opinion, both senses of separating into sides.

clue.text: One way to check payment by cheque

definitions.text: One way to check payment by cheque

parts.words: One way to check payment by cheque
parts.note: to check here is to hold back: writing a later date on a cheque stops it being cashed until then

explanation.surface: A tip for verifying that a cheque payment has gone through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' looks like verify, but it means delay or restrain, as in checking someone's progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing a future date on a cheque means the bank cannot honour it until that day, delaying payment.

clue.text: Tangled threads are the most difficult

indicators.note: tangled thread is twisted out of order, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Knotted threads are the trickiest thing to sort out.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of a word meaning tough or difficult.

clue.text: A lieutenant bearing one star

parts.note: an air is a manner or bearing, as in an air of confidence

explanation.surface: A junior officer wears a single star on his shoulder.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests rank insignia; 'one star' is in fact the definition, a named star in the constellation Aquila.
explanation.definitionFit: Altair is the brightest star in the constellation Aquila, the Eagle.

clue.text: In this way a West African country becomes East African

parts.note: so means thus or in this manner
Mali is a landlocked country in West Africa

explanation.surface: A geography puzzle: how a nation in the west turns into one in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: A Somali is a native of Somalia, on the Horn of Africa in the east of the continent.

clue.text: A non-specialist graduate, I perform autumn jobs

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate
to do is to perform, as in do a play
fall is the American word for autumn
work means tasks or jobs to be done

explanation.surface: A graduate describes the seasonal jobs they do, raking leaves perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'I perform autumn jobs' as a sentence, but each word is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A servant who did every kind of household chore, rather than one specialised task.

clue.text: Mass in its full version

parts.note: Mass. is the postal abbreviation of a US state, so writing it out in full gives the state's name

explanation.surface: A church service performed without any cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' looks like the church service; it is the short form of an American state name.
explanation.definitionFit: Mass. is the standard abbreviation for this New England state, so its full form is the state's name.

clue.text: Champions away from home?

parts.note: champions are medieval warriors who fought for a cause, and away from home suggests wandering

explanation.surface: A sports team that wins its away fixtures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champions' suggests sporting winners and 'away from home' an away match; in fact they are wandering chivalric heroes.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval warriors who roamed in search of adventure, defending causes as champions of the weak.

clue.text: A fool it's wrong to help

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: wrong means put out of order, so the letters of the word before are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone warns that helping a fool is a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: To aid someone is to give them help.

clue.text: Sort of society in which people want to take part?

definitions.text: Sort of society in which people want to take part?

parts.words: Sort of society in which people want to take part?
parts.note: take part is read as wanting a part, a role in a play, as members of an amateur theatre group do

explanation.surface: A club whose members are keen to get involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take part' sounds like simply joining in, but the members want parts in a stage production.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur theatre club is called this kind of society, and its members audition for roles.

clue.text: Expected a letter from a duke

indicators.note: a single letter is taken away from the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone awaiting correspondence from an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A letter from' looks like correspondence; it means one letter is removed, here the K from DUKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something anticipated at a certain time is said to be due, as in the train is due.

clue.text: Team held by mother to be the tops

indicators.note: held by means contained within the word for mother

parts.note: mama is a word for mother
XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: A mother hugging her winning team as the best of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Maxima, plural of maximum, are the highest points or peaks.

clue.text: Honest deal?

definitions.meaning: a poker hand of five cards in consecutive order, as dealt

explanation.surface: A request for a fair bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the card-game sense of the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means upright and frank, and also a poker hand of five cards in sequence.

clue.text: A church is one

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A remark that a church counts as one of something.
explanation.definitionFit: In cards and dice the ace counts as the single, the number one.

clue.text: TV line between Britain and France

definitions.meaning: a television station broadcasting on one band
the strait of water separating England from France

explanation.surface: A television station broadcasting across the water between two countries.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a broadcasting station and the English sea strait that divides Britain from France.

clue.text: Pan back to a card-game

indicators.note: back means the word before it is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: A camera pans back across a card table.
explanation.walkthrough: In 'Pan back', 'Pan' looks like a camera movement, but it is the word to turn round.
explanation.definitionFit: Nap, short for Napoleon, is a trick-taking card game.

clue.text: He needs a regular supply of drugs to keep going

definitions.text: He needs a regular supply of drugs to keep going

parts.words: He needs a regular supply of drugs to keep going
parts.note: sounds like a drug addict, but the drugs are stock for a pharmacy business

explanation.surface: A portrait of someone dependent on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints an addict; the person is a pharmacist whose shop needs restocking. In Britain a chemist is a pharmacist's shop or the pharmacist.
explanation.definitionFit: A British pharmacist dispenses medicines and must keep the shop stocked with them.

clue.text: All being well, it should be empty

definitions.text: All being well, it should be empty

parts.words: All being well, it should be empty
parts.note: all being well is read literally: if everyone is healthy, nobody needs a bed in this institution

explanation.surface: A hopeful remark about something that ought to be vacant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All being well' is usually an idiom for 'if things go to plan'; here it means everyone is healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: If everyone is in good health, no patients need the wards, so they stay empty.

clue.text: Male bird and plant

parts.note: man is a male person
a drake is a male duck

explanation.surface: A list: a male duck and a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandrake is a Mediterranean herb with a forked root, steeped in folklore.

clue.text: Resistance to mal-de-mer, say, among swimmers

indicators.note: among means placed inside the word for the swimmers

parts.note: seals are swimming marine mammals
eg, for example, is what say means here

explanation.surface: Swimmers who are immune to seasickness.
explanation.walkthrough: Mal de mer is French for seasickness.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has found their sea-legs no longer suffers from seasickness on board.

clue.text: Prank ceased being funny when father came in

indicators.note: came in means entered the middle of the jumbled letters
funny means strange or odd, so the letters of ceased are put in an odd order

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: A joke stopped being amusing once Dad arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' looks like describing the prank as amusing; 'being funny' is the anagram signal on 'ceased', and 'came in' sends father inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild or mischievous adventure, a caper or prank.

clue.text: No way out around the centre, at all events

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters wrap round what follows
out means put out of order, so the letters of no way are scrambled
the centre of a three-letter word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Advice that there is no exit round the middle, in any case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns NO WAY into ANYOW; 'around' puts it round H, the centre of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean in any case or regardless, synonyms for whatever happens.

clue.text: Bill joins a spy organisation, becoming a plant

parts.note: ac, account, is a bill
the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency

explanation.surface: A man named Bill joins the intelligence services and turns out to be a mole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a plant' sounds like a spy planted inside an organisation, fitting the surface; it is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Acacia is a tree or shrub, the wattle, with feathery leaves.

clue.text: Soldier dispatched to the lines

parts.note: sent means dispatched
RY, railway, is the lines a train runs on

explanation.surface: A soldier sent off to the front lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is a soldier posted to keep guard.

clue.text: Current term for" a politician

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Current word for a politician, as of today.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like topical; it is electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampere is the unit of electric current, shortened in speech.

clue.text: Contradictory orders to the yachtsman for more canvas

definitions.text: Contradictory orders to the yachtsman for more canvas

parts.words: Contradictory orders to the yachtsman for more canvas
parts.note: two opposite commands, one to remain and one to set off by boat, combine into an extra piece of rigging

explanation.surface: A sailor is given conflicting instructions about adding sail.
explanation.walkthrough: The two orders are 'stay' and 'sail', which contradict each other; together they name an extra sail.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangular fore-and-aft sail set on a stay, adding sail area to a yacht.

clue.text: Raid the entrance?

definitions.meaning: read as a road leading in, a way of entry

explanation.surface: A question about raiding a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the whimsical second sense: a road in.
explanation.definitionFit: An incursion or advance into hostile ground, and, read playfully, a road leading in.

clue.text: The tobacco habit?

parts.note: habit is read as clothing, as a monk's habit, worn while having a pipe or cigar

explanation.surface: A reference to the addiction to nicotine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' looks like an addiction; it means a garment, as in a nun's habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A velvet jacket once worn by gentlemen while smoking, a garment for the smoking ritual.
